home.title: Build Anki decks from code
home.description: Build Basic, Cloze, Image Occlusion and custom Anki cards with Rust, TypeScript or Python. Package media, keep note identities stable and review deck updates.
home.intro: Anki Forge is an open-source Anki APKG generation library with a Rust core and Rust, Python and Node.js interfaces. Package media, use custom templates and review updates before distribution.
home.install: Export spanish.apkg with the public {version} package. Normal export needs no Anki installation.
home.try: See the code. Try the card.
home.tryDescription: Switch between runnable Rust examples, flip the previews, and download the decks they produce.
home.evolveDescription: Correct a definition or add an example. Stable IDs and a previous build help Anki Forge match existing notes when you export again.
home.validateDescription: Inspect diagnostics for missing fields, media, and template problems. Make validation part of your build.
home.templateDescription: Start with Basic and Cloze, or define your own note types. Keep HTML, CSS, and media in reusable template bundles.
home.nextTitle: From your first deck to the next update
home.nextDescription: Build three cards from shared JSON, image and audio inputs. Keep your business IDs, change an answer, and review the update against the original APKG.

examples.title: Card examples
examples.description: Explore Basic, Cloze, media, and Image Occlusion cards built with Anki Forge. Read their Rust source and download the generated Anki decks.
examples.intro: Explore the source, flip the cards, and open the generated decks in Anki. These web previews use the same fields as the downloads.
examples.updateDescription: The second build changes the answer from “hello” to “hello; hi”. It compares against the first package and checks that the note identity is preserved.
examples.limitations: Anki’s import settings and local edits affect how updates are applied. The previews show content and identity; card styling and review behavior come from Anki.
examples.basic: A Spanish greeting with a question, an answer, and an explicit stable ID. Start here for simple front-and-back cards.
examples.cloze: Hide a word in context with Anki’s cloze syntax. This note has one deletion, so it generates one card.
examples.media: An image and a playable tone, packaged with the note. This excerpt uses an ear-training note type defined in the full source.
examples.occlusion: A keyed rectangle hides the nucleus in an illustrated cell cross section. The downloadable deck uses the same image and mask as this preview.

machine.intro: Anki Forge generates Anki APKG decks from code using Rust, Node / TypeScript or Python.
machine.constraints: Normal export does not require Anki. Published package APIs differ from source builds. Keep the original previous distribution APKG for updates; Anki import settings and newer local edits can affect the result.
